title: Delhi ITAT: Returning NRI's Dubai Life Insurance Policy Not an Undisclosed Asset Under the Black Money Act
case_name: Sarvesh Naidu v. Deputy Director of Income Tax (Investigation)-1
card_summary: The taxpayer funded a Dubai policy partly from tax-exempt non-resident Dubai salary and partly, after returning to India, from taxable Indian salary; it matured in 2016 for about USD 52,896.76. The Tribunal deleted a Rs 40.03 lakh Black Money Act addition, relying on CBDT Circular No. 13 of 2015 to hold the policy was not an undisclosed asset, and held Section 10(10D) is not limited to Indian insurers.
card_tip: A foreign life insurance policy funded from genuinely non-taxable foreign income during an NRI's non-resident years is not an undisclosed asset merely because the insurer is foreign; keep the funding trail to show it.
verification_notes: The mixed Dubai and Indian-salary funding of the policy, the 2016 maturity figure of USD 52,896.76, the Rs 40.03 lakh addition deleted, the reliance on CBDT Circular 13/2015, the Section 10(10D) holding, and the 31 July 2026 order date (AY 2017-18) are corroborated across TaxGuru, A2Z Taxcorp and TaxCorp reports of the same ITAT Delhi order.
